rationale: Authority and scope: pass. Primary plan matches registered exact identity. Current context supplies approved original and directory Design Reviews; relocated Validation remains the approved governing contract, including TEST-SR-01–14, VAL-SR-01–18 and source maps. The completed directory plan/work retains its original identities and review meaning; five distinct validation-m1 through validation-m5 items allocate only remaining work.

Requirement traceability: pass. The Requirements covered table maps every VAL-SR and scoped TEST group to milestones and TG-CACHE/EXEC/COMPOSE/CASES/ADOPT/FINAL. Stable SYS/ENG/SKL composition obligations join M5 rather than reopening unselected product features. Every milestone identifies governing requirements, concrete components, dependencies, required command groups, completion outcome, review handoff and recovery.

Sequencing: pass. M1 retires cache/measurement before isolation auditing; M2 extracts selected execution into the Design-named internal module with graph/process proof; M3 composes broad/main into that engine and retires historical runtime readers; M4 enables audited real cases; M5 completes source and public-consumer adoption with packed-product proof. Temporary dual scheduling exists only as an explicit intermediate state before M3. Independent milestone review and correction closure separate slices.

Cache and retirement protection: pass. TG-CACHE observes actual repeated execution including second-run failure, no-write retired-input rejection and preserved current v3 negatives. Default-cache deletion requires a fresh no-symlink/content inspection, while arbitrary caches and historical evidence remain untouched. Exact seven specification/test-specification pairs, cache ADR, cache helper/test/measurement functionality, classification checker/readers and redundant scheduler membership are mapped to retained proof or explicit retirement. Mixed source remainders, immutable old evidence and unknown protection remain protected. TEST-SR-14 prior scope is explicitly separate from VAL-SR-13.

Executor proof: pass. TG-EXEC allocates complete prelaunch closed-vocabulary and graph validation, trusted command basis, missing/cyclic dependencies, resource/isolation conflicts, stable output and first-required-failure meaning, fail-fast unfinished work, positive overrides/defaults, controlled child/grandchild cleanup, five-second grace, unavailable/invalid result paths and unrelated-resource preservation. Real wrapper/module boundary proof complements process fixtures; a success mock or self-derived expected result is not sufficient.

Composition proof: pass. TG-COMPOSE preserves distinct mode/phase identity, preflight and focused gating, diagnostic failure origin, deleted/shared source selection, reason-preserving deduplication, Release check-ci interception and shared build/validation output with explicit success dependency. Actual jobs=1 and jobs=2 broad runs supplement isolated wrapper regressions. Runtime operation with historical classifications absent and override rejection demonstrate removal rather than mere changed documentation.

Case adoption: pass. M4 explicitly audits normal loaders/custom hooks, class/module/setup state, fixtures, environment, nested subprocess demand and external resources for all three selected real suites. It requires each surviving case through its original Class.test_method selector, complete direct/individual/sequential/concurrent discovered-started-completed set agreement, actual overlap and diagnostic preservation. Remaining justified external constraints may serialize; metadata-only changes, universal serial declaration and unaudited populations cannot satisfy completion. Ordinary ordered scenarios remain one independent case.

Command feasibility and observation boundaries: pass. Existing named lifecycle/metadata/selector, skill/resource, model, adapter/npm and full CLI test entrypoints are concrete repository commands; only explicitly allocated test-validation-execution.py is new. Direct source inspection corroborates current cache dispatch, embedded selected/broad scheduling and historical baseline readers. C4 owns controlled graph/process/three-suite integration, while C5/C6/C7/C8/C10 prove real composed candidates. Conditional C9 retains Release authority without live publication. No new public discovery service or runner CLI is invented.

Consumer and product integration: pass. M5 names current governance/model readers, ten existing skill consumers, shared source and projections, FU-012 and actual generated archives/packed CLI. TG-ADOPT preserves selectively loaded portable criteria and optional individual-skill CLI use, resource/hash parity, actual command/record/installation boundaries and separate assessment/publication authority. Canonical correction and regeneration precede candidate claims; unknown live readers block removal.

Final closeout: pass. TG-FINAL and a distinct lifecycle checkpoint require all directory and five Validation milestones/corrections, fresh independent final whole-change Code Review of the complete hierarchy/directory/Validation diff and interactions, then separate Verify of current source/generated/evidence authority. Earlier reviews or passing local subsets cannot replace these gates. Failed proof remains failed until an owned correction or supported applicability disposition.

Boundaries and recovery: pass. All eight Validation dimensions and combined hazards have group-level allocation. Coherent source/reader/test restoration preserves unrelated and historical state; jobs=1 cannot conceal missing semantics. Unknown behavior or a new public interface routes to Design, while settled fixture/isolation correction remains M4. No speed threshold, new ledger, hosted worker, cache replacement, publication or customer-governance adoption is authorized.

No material Delivery findings remain. This independently recorded plan approval supports only the requested authoring/review handoff; root retains workflow routing and the user-selected execution boundary.
